newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain to cut official rate on Friday - poll.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain to cut official rate on Friday - poll.

text.p: The Bank of Spain is expected to cut its six percent money market rate at its regular repurchase auction on Friday, dealers said on Thursday.

A Reuter poll conducted after the release of better-than-expected February CPI, showed that seven out of ten were expecting a rate cut of at least 25 basis points with one analyst suggesting a cut of up to 50 basis points.
February CPI fell 0.1 percent from January for a 2.5 percent year-on-year versus a 2.9 percent rise one month ago.
The market consensus was pointing to 2.7/2.8 percent.
February CPI set a record low since 1969.
After such an improvement, analysts said that government's goal to end the year with a CPI rate at 2.6 percent year on year is drawing closer.
The three analysts rule out a cut, saying the relatively weak peseta was a factor suggesting a more cautious approach by the Bank of Spain.
The Bank of Spain last cut on January 16, when the key money market rate was reduced by 25 basis points to six percent.
The Bank of Spain started the current cycle of rate reductions on December 22, 1995, when it cut its official rate to nine pct from 9.25 percent.
